        (TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianSmoothing.gaussianSmoothing (πbar p) (Real.sqrt t)).map R =
          TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianSmoothing.gaussianSmoothing (π p) (Real.sqrt (t/c))) ∧

        TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance νbar
          (TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianSmoothing.gaussianSmoothing (πbar p) (Real.sqrt t)) ^ 2 ≤
            ENNReal.ofReal B →
        TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance (νbar.map R)
          (TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianSmoothing.gaussianSmoothing (π p) (Real.sqrt (t/c))) ^ 2 ≤

    (hw : TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance ν

  let A := η+τ
  let a := (α:ℝ)+A⁻¹
  let c := (β:ℝ)+A⁻¹
  let k := c/a
  let u := fun p : E × E => p.1+Real.sqrt τ • p.2
  let F := fun p x => U x+A⁻¹/2*‖x-u p‖^2
  let T := fun p x => x-c⁻¹ • gradient (F p) x
  let N := actualIndex T (fun p x => ‖gradient (F p) x‖^2) (a*d)
  let out := fun p => (T p)^[N p] p.1
  let S := fun x : E => Real.sqrt c • x
  let R := fun x : E => (Real.sqrt c)⁻¹ • x
  let G := fun p x => F p (R x)

  have ha : 0 < a := add_pos_of_nonneg_of_pos α.coe_nonneg (inv_pos.mpr hA)
  have hc : 0 < c := add_pos_of_nonneg_of_pos β.coe_nonneg (inv_pos.mpr hA)

              Complete source statement (Samplinglib restatement)

              There exist a Markov joint kernel J:S->(E x S) and a Markov absorbed transition P:S->S. For every s, J_s is the pushforward of M_s product gamma_E by (x,z) -> (obs(s,(x,z)),U(s,(x,z))). Its first marginal is exactly G(M_s,sqrt(tau_s/(beta+b))). The kernel identity J.fst compProd J.condKernel=J holds. For each s, for J.fst_s-almost every y, for J.condKernel(s,y)-almost every t, t.precision=bp_s and t.center=bp_s^(-1)*(b*u+v_s^(-1)*y). For every actual Markov R:S->E, every s and every measurable A, the nonnegative integral of R(U(s,(x,z)),A) under M_s product gamma_E equals the iterated nonnegative integral of R(t,A) first under J.condKernel(s,y), then under J.fst_s. P_s is dirac_s when threshold<=b and the pushforward by U otherwise. If b<threshold, (R composed with P)(s,A) equals the same conditional iterated integral.

              • E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space of positive dimension d. V:E->R is C2 and its genuine Hessian satisfies alpha*norm(w)^2 <= D2V(x)[w,w] <= beta*norm(w)^2 for all x,w. The nonnegative reals alpha,beta satisfy0<alpha<=beta.
              • The full state is S=NNReal x E x E x Nat x (Nat->E), written s=(b,u,xref,k,history). M:S->E is an actual Markov kernel. eta,tau:S->R are measurable and strictly positive at every state; they may depend on all coordinates. Fix any nonnegative precision threshold. No source schedule,initial-reference admissibility,history origin,accuracy or moment assumption is imposed.
              • Put v_s=(eta_s+tau_s)/(beta+b), bp_s=b+toNNReal(v_s^(-1)), and obs(s,(x,z))=x+sqrt(tau_s/(beta+b))*z. The next center is center(s,(x,z))=bp_s^(-1)*(b*u+v_s^(-1)*obs(s,(x,z))). The observation variance tau_s/(beta+b) is distinct from the RGO update variance v_s.
              • Define F_p(w)=V(w)+bp_s/2*norm(w-center(p))^2 and T_p(w)=w-(beta+bp_s)^(-1)*grad F_p(w), where p=(s,(x,z)). N_p is the least n with norm(grad F_p(T_p^n(x)))^2 <= (alpha+bp_s)*d, or zero if none exists. The actual update is U(p)=(bp_s,center(p),T_p^N_p(x),k+1,prepend(obs(p),history)). It uses the pre-noise sample x to initialize GD, and retains the full reference and history.
              • gamma_E denotes standard Gaussian measure. Gaussian smoothing G(mu,sigma) is the pushforward of mu product the law of sigma*Z under addition. J.fst denotes the observation marginal of a joint kernel J:S->(E x S). J.condKernel is the parameterized Markov conditional state kernel (s,y)->S supplied by standard-Borel disintegration. R composed with P means first draw a state from P and then an output from R.

              Actual conditional execution

              \[J_s=(\mathrm{obs}_s,U_s)_\#(M_s\otimes\gamma_E)=Q_s\otimes C_s,\qquad (R\circ P)(s,A)=\int\!\int R(t,A)\,C(s,y,dt)\,Q_s(dy)\quad(b_s< b_*).\]

              Read this first

              Mathematical statement

              There exist a Markov joint kernel J:S->(E x S) and a Markov absorbed transition P:S->S. For every s, J_s is the pushforward of M_s product gamma_E by (x,z) -> (obs(s,(x,z)),U(s,(x,z))). Its first marginal is exactly G(M_s,sqrt(tau_s/(beta+b))). The kernel identity J.fst compProd J.condKernel=J holds. For each s, for J.fst_s-almost every y, for J.condKernel(s,y)-almost every t, t.precision=bp_s and t.center=bp_s^(-1)*(b*u+v_s^(-1)*y). For every actual Markov R:S->E, every s and every measurable A, the nonnegative integral of R(U(s,(x,z)),A) under M_s product gamma_E equals the iterated nonnegative integral of R(t,A) first under J.condKernel(s,y), then under J.fst_s. P_s is dirac_s when threshold<=b and the pushforward by U otherwise. If b<threshold, (R composed with P)(s,A) equals the same conditional iterated integral.

              \[J_s=(\mathrm{obs}_s,U_s)_\#(M_s\otimes\gamma_E)=Q_s\otimes C_s,\qquad (R\circ P)(s,A)=\int\!\int R(t,A)\,C(s,y,dt)\,Q_s(dy)\quad(b_s< b_*).\]

              Proof roadmap

              1. 1Keep the exact pre-noise reference update

                Apply ReferenceCarryingKernel under the genuine Hessian assumptions. Its measurable update contains the true first inner GD hit from x, the precision-weighted center, and the complete reference/count/history. The private firstIndex definition is definitionally the same fallback/least-hit function as the parent. No reference is supplied as a free observation-only function.

              2. 2Build one joint observation and updated-state law

                Set Q=M times the constant standard Gaussian kernel. Pair the input state with this draw using the identity kernel, then push forward by the measurable pair (obs,update). Both coordinates therefore refer to the same x,z. The product and measurable-map kernel instances prove the resulting J is Markov.

              3. 3Identify the actual observation marginal

                Project the joint pushforward onto its first coordinate. Composition of measurable maps removes update while preserving the actual observation x+sigma_s*z. The product pushforward identity moves Gaussian scaling into its noise marginal, giving the existing GaussianSmoothing definition exactly. No Wasserstein or KL assumption is used.

              4. 4Disintegrate jointly in state and observation

                The full state has a standard Borel structure and is nonempty, and the finite-dimensional observation space is countably generated. The finite Markov J therefore has a parameterized Markov conditional kernel on (s,y). Mathlib disintegrate gives a kernel identity, not separate nonmeasurable choices of a conditional measure for each s.

              5. 5Recover deterministic precision and center only almost everywhere

                Under the actual joint pushforward the next precision and center equal their source formulas for every original x,z. Their equality event is measurable. Transfer its full measure through the map, rewrite J by its disintegration, and apply the kernel AE Fubini direction. This gives the nested AE statement; conditional versions on null observation fibers are not constrained.

              6. 6Factor any actual remaining output

                For measurable A the function (y,t)->R(t,A) is measurable and nonnegative. Integrate it against the disintegration and then rewrite the same J as the actual joint pushforward. The nonnegative compProd/map formulas yield the equality without a finite moment or integrability premise. R may depend on the retained reference and history.

              7. 7Connect the absorbed execution on its active branch

                Take the actual P constructed by ReferenceCarryingKernel. At b<threshold its law is precisely the update pushforward. The kernel composition integral and the measurable map formula reduce (R composed with P)(s,A) to the preceding equality. At terminal states P is a self-loop, so no such identification with hypothetical continuing J is asserted.

Mathlib disintegrate gives a kernel identity, not separate nonmeasurable choices of a conditional measure for each s.

Transfer its full measure through the map, rewrite J by its disintegration, and apply the kernel AE Fubini direction. This gives the nested AE statement; conditional versions on null observation fibers are not constrained.

The nonnegative compProd/map formulas yield the equality without a finite moment or integrability premise. R may depend on the retained reference and history.

              theorem observation_conditional_kernel {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0}
    (hα : 0 < α) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x w : E, (α:ℝ)*‖w‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x w w ∧
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x w w ≤ (β:ℝ)*‖w‖^2)
    (hd : 0 < (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ))
    (η τ : RefState E → ℝ) (hη : Measurable η) (hτ : Measurable τ)
    (hη0 : ∀ s, 0 < η s) (hτ0 : ∀ s, 0 < τ s)
    (M : Kernel (RefState E) E) [IsMarkovKernel M] (threshold : ℝ≥0) :
    let d : ℝ := Module.finrank ℝ E
    let v := fun s : RefState E => (η s+τ s)/((β:ℝ)+s.1)
    let bp := fun s : RefState E => s.1+Real.toNNReal (v s)⁻¹
    let obs := fun p : RefState E × (E × E) => p.2.1+Real.sqrt (τ p.1/((β:ℝ)+p.1.1)) • p.2.2
    let center := fun p : RefState E × (E × E) => (bp p.1:ℝ)⁻¹ •
      ((p.1.1:ℝ) • p.1.2.1+(v p.1)⁻¹ • obs p)
    let F := fun p x => V x+(bp p.1:ℝ)/2*‖x-center p‖^2
    let T := fun p x => x-((β:ℝ)+bp p.1)⁻¹ • gradient (F p) x
    let q := fun n p => ‖gradient (F p) ((T p)^[n] p.2.1)‖^2
    let N := firstIndex q (fun p => ((α:ℝ)+bp p.1)*d)
    let out := fun p => (T p)^[N p] p.2.1
    let update := fun p : RefState E × (E × E) =>
      (bp p.1,center p,out p,p.1.2.2.2.1+1,fun n => Nat.casesOn n (obs p) p.1.2.2.2.2)
    ∃ J : Kernel (RefState E) (E × RefState E), ∃ hJ : IsMarkovKernel J,
      letI := hJ
      (∀ s, J s = ((M s).prod (stdGaussian E)).map
        (fun z => (obs (s,z),update (s,z)))) ∧
      (∀ s, J.fst s =
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianSmoothing.gaussianSmoothing
          (M s) (Real.sqrt (τ s/((β:ℝ)+s.1)))) ∧
      J.fst ⊗ₖ J.condKernel = J ∧
      (∀ s, ∀ᵐ y ∂J.fst s, ∀ᵐ t ∂J.condKernel (s,y),
        t.1=bp s ∧ t.2.1=(bp s:ℝ)⁻¹ • ((s.1:ℝ) • s.2.1+(v s)⁻¹ • y)) ∧
      (∀ (R : Kernel (RefState E) E) [IsMarkovKernel R] (s : RefState E)
        (A : Set E), MeasurableSet A →
        (∫⁻ z, R (update (s,z)) A ∂(M s).prod (stdGaussian E)) =
        ∫⁻ y, ∫⁻ t, R t A ∂J.condKernel (s,y) ∂J.fst s) ∧
      ∃ P : Kernel (RefState E) (RefState E), ∃ hP : IsMarkovKernel P,
        letI := hP
        (∀ s, P s=if threshold ≤ s.1 then Measure.dirac s else
          ((M s).prod (stdGaussian E)).map (fun z => update (s,z))) ∧
        ∀ (R : Kernel (RefState E) E) [IsMarkovKernel R] (s : RefState E),
          s.1 < threshold → ∀ A : Set E, MeasurableSet A →
          (R ∘ₖ P) s A = ∫⁻ y, ∫⁻ t, R t A ∂J.condKernel (s,y) ∂J.fst s

    ∃ J : Kernel (RefState E) (E × RefState E), ∃ hJ : IsMarkovKernel J,
      letI := hJ

        t.1=bp s ∧ t.2.1=(bp s:ℝ)⁻¹ • ((s.1:ℝ) • s.2.1+(v s)⁻¹ • y)) ∧
      (∀ (R : Kernel (RefState E) E) [IsMarkovKernel R] (s : RefState E)

        (∫⁻ z, R (update (s,z)) A ∂(M s).prod (stdGaussian E)) =

  intro d v bp obs center F T q N out update
  obtain ⟨J,hJ,hJs,hJfst,hdis,hsupp,hfactor⟩ :=

  let := hJ
  have href := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ReferenceCarryingKernel.reference_carrying_kernel

  have hu : Measurable update := href.2.2.2.1
  obtain ⟨P,hP,hPs,hproj⟩ := href.2.2.2.2.2
  let := hP
  refine ⟨J,hJ,hJs,hJfst,hdis,hsupp,hfactor,P,hP,hPs,?_⟩
  intro R hR s hs A hA
  rw [Kernel.comp_apply' R P s hA,hPs s,if_neg (not_le.mpr hs)]

              Samplinglib mathematical lesson

              The squared norm of a standard Gaussian has mean d

              AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.StdGaussianMoment.integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian · theorem · Teaching coverage

              Read this first

              Mathematical statement

              If Z is standard Gaussian in E, then its squared norm is Bochner-integrable and its expectation is the real dimension of E.

              \[\mathbb E\|Z\|^2=\dim_{\mathbb R}E.\]

              Proof roadmap

              1. 1Obtain genuine L2 integrability

                Mathlib proves that the identity random variable belongs to L2 under the standard Gaussian law. The L2-to-integrable-square equivalence therefore gives integrability of the squared norm before any coordinate sum is exchanged with the integral.

              2. 2Compute every directional variance

                For an orthonormal basis vector e_i, the covariance identity and zero Gaussian mean give E<e_i,Z>²=1. Each scalar square is dominated by ‖Z‖², so it is integrable.

              3. 3Apply finite-dimensional Parseval

                Parseval writes the squared norm as the finite sum of directional squares. Since every summand is integrable, the integral commutes with the finite sum and each term contributes one.

              Full assumptions and notation

              All objects and hypotheses

              • E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra.
              • The probability law is Mathlib's actual standard Gaussian stdGaussian E; no abstract covariance hypothesis replaces it.

              Mathematical proof

              1. Obtain genuine L2 integrability

              Mathlib proves that the identity random variable belongs to L2 under the standard Gaussian law. The L2-to-integrable-square equivalence therefore gives integrability of the squared norm before any coordinate sum is exchanged with the integral.

              \[Z\in L^2(\gamma_E)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|Z\|^2\in L^1(\gamma_E).\]
              Corresponding Lean step

              IsGaussian.memLp_two_id and memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm produce hi.

              2. Compute every directional variance

              For an orthonormal basis vector e_i, the covariance identity and zero Gaussian mean give E<e_i,Z>²=1. Each scalar square is dominated by ‖Z‖², so it is integrable.

              \[\mathbb E\langle e_i,Z\rangle^2=1,\qquad |\langle e_i,Z\rangle|^2\le\|Z\|^2.\]
              Corresponding Lean step

              covarianceBilin_apply, covarianceBilin_stdGaussian and integral_id_stdGaussian prove hdir; norm_inner_le_norm supplies hL1.

              3. Apply finite-dimensional Parseval

              Parseval writes the squared norm as the finite sum of directional squares. Since every summand is integrable, the integral commutes with the finite sum and each term contributes one.

              \[\mathbb E\|Z\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^{d}\mathbb E\langle e_i,Z\rangle^2=\sum_{i=1}^{d}1=d.\]
              Corresponding Lean step

              stdOrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_norm_inner_right and integral_finsetSum close the calculation.

              theorem integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] :

              Exact module and namespace context

              Lean proof · integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian

              ASTIS packages existing Mathlib Gaussian L2/covariance facts through finite-dimensional Parseval; it introduces no new axiom or source-specific assumption.

              Braces mark parameters Lean can infer; square brackets request structures such as a measurable space or probability measure. Named hypotheses are mathematical premises, not facts established by this declaration. Section parameters are described in the mathematical hypotheses above; the module link retains their exact source context.

              theorem integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] :
    Integrable (fun x : E => ‖x‖ ^ 2) (stdGaussian E) ∧
      (∫ x : E, ‖x‖ ^ 2 ∂stdGaussian E) = Module.finrank ℝ E := by
  classical
  have hi : Integrable (fun x : E => ‖x‖ ^ 2) (stdGaussian E) :=
    (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm (by fun_prop)).1 IsGaussian.memLp_two_id
  let b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E
  have hdir (i) : (∫ x : E, (inner ℝ (b i) x) ^ 2 ∂stdGaussian E) = 1 := by
    have hh := covarianceBilin_apply (μ := stdGaussian E)
      IsGaussian.memLp_two_id (b i) (b i)
    rw [covarianceBilin_stdGaussian] at hh
    change inner ℝ (b i) (b i) = _ at hh
    simpa [integral_id_stdGaussian, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq,
      b.orthonormal.norm_eq_one, pow_two] using hh.symm
  have hL1 (i) : Integrable (fun x : E => (inner ℝ (b i) x) ^ 2)
      (stdGaussian E) := by
    apply hi.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards with x
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    have hb := norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) (b i) x
    rw [b.orthonormal.norm_eq_one, one_mul] at hb
    have hsq := (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg (inner ℝ (b i) x)) (norm_nonneg x)).2 hb
    simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs] using hsq
  refine ⟨hi, ?_⟩
  calc
    (∫ x : E, ‖x‖ ^ 2 ∂stdGaussian E) =
        ∫ x : E, ∑ i, (inner ℝ (b i) x) ^ 2 ∂stdGaussian E := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs] using (b.sum_sq_norm_inner_right x).symm
    _ = ∑ i, ∫ x : E, (inner ℝ (b i) x) ^ 2 ∂stdGaussian E :=
      integral_finsetSum _ (fun i _ => hL1 i)
    _ = Module.finrank ℝ E := by simp [hdir]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.StdGaussianMoment

                arXiv:2609.06906v1 · Algorithm 3.1 lines 282–300; Lemma D.4 proof lines 2177–2180 · faithful paraphrase

                Complete source statement (Samplinglib restatement)

                Adjoin a fresh standard Gaussian to the incoming phase-state law and perform Algorithm 3.1's first OU half-refresh. The refreshed state is measurable and square-integrable, and its exact second moment contains the additional Gaussian term (1−exp(−h))d.

                • A probability law nu on incoming (X,Pinit), with integrable combined squared distance to (x*,0) and expectation at most M.
                • A nonnegative phase length h and a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel state space.
                • Fresh standard Gaussian momentum noise represented by nu.prod(stdGaussian E).

                Actual refresh

                \[P_0=e^{-h/2}P_{\rm init}+\sqrt{1-e^{-h}}\,Z,\qquad Z\sim N(0,I_d)\text{ fresh}.\]

                Exact and bounded moment

                \[\mathbb E[\|X-x_*\|^2+\|P_0\|^2]=\mathbb E[\|X-x_*\|^2+e^{-h}\|P_{\rm init}\|^2]+(1-e^{-h})d\le M+(1-e^{-h})d.\]

                Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                The actual OU half-refresh and its corrected moment budget

                AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PartialMomentumRefresh.partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment · theorem · Teaching coverage

                Read this first

                Mathematical statement

                Set a=exp(−h/2), sigma=sqrt(1−exp(−h)), X0=X and P0=a Pinit+sigma Z on the product law of the incoming state and a fresh standard Gaussian. Then X0 and P0 are measurable, their combined squared distance is integrable, and its expectation satisfies the exact identity and corrected budget below.

                \[\mathbb E[\|X_0-x_*\|^2+\|P_0\|^2]=\mathbb E[\|X-x_*\|^2+e^{-h}\|P_{\rm init}\|^2]+(1-e^{-h})d\le M+(1-e^{-h})d.\]

                Proof roadmap

                1. 1Realize the fresh draw by a product law

                  A sample is a pair ((X,Pinit),Z) distributed according to nu⊗gamma_d. The first coordinate is the incoming phase state and the second is a genuinely fresh standard Gaussian. Coordinate projections and continuous linear combinations make X0 and P0 measurable.

                2. 2Establish every integrability premise

                  Nonnegativity lets us extract the position and momentum square integrability from the combined incoming energy. L2 then gives integrability of Pinit itself. The shared ASTIS theorem gives ‖Z‖² in L1, while Mathlib's Gaussian integrability API separately gives Z in L1; together these make the mixed inner product integrable on the product measure.

                3. 3Use actual independence to kill the cross term

                  For every fixed incoming momentum, the Gaussian mean is zero. Fubini is legal because the mixed inner product was proved integrable, hence its expectation under the product law vanishes without a centering assumption on Pinit.

                4. 4Expand the refreshed square

                  The coefficients satisfy a²=e^(−h) and sigma²=1−e^(−h). Expanding the Hilbert norm, integrating the four integrable terms, using the zero cross term and E‖Z‖²=d gives the exact identity.

                5. 5Derive the consumer-ready bound

                  Because h≥0, 0<e^(−h)≤1. Replacing the damped momentum term by the incoming momentum square and applying the input budget yields M+(1−e^(−h))d. The extra dimension term must remain visible until the later paper-parameter absorption step.

                Full assumptions and notation

                All objects and hypotheses

                • The incoming phase-state law nu on E×E is a probability measure, and the combined square ‖X−x*‖²+‖Pinit‖² is integrable with expectation at most M.
                • E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space and h≥0.
                • Freshness of Z~N(0,I) is represented by the actual product measure nu⊗stdGaussian(E), rather than by assuming the mixed term has expectation zero.

                Mathematical proof

                1. Realize the fresh draw by a product law

                A sample is a pair ((X,Pinit),Z) distributed according to nu⊗gamma_d. The first coordinate is the incoming phase state and the second is a genuinely fresh standard Gaussian. Coordinate projections and continuous linear combinations make X0 and P0 measurable.

                \[\mu=\nu\otimes\gamma_d,\qquad P_0=e^{-h/2}P_{\rm init}+\sqrt{1-e^{-h}}\,Z.\]
                Corresponding Lean step

                The public X and P0 lets use product projections; the final fun_prop goals prove their measurability.

                2. Establish every integrability premise

                Nonnegativity lets us extract the position and momentum square integrability from the combined incoming energy. L2 then gives integrability of Pinit itself. The shared ASTIS theorem gives ‖Z‖² in L1, while Mathlib's Gaussian integrability API separately gives Z in L1; together these make the mixed inner product integrable on the product measure.

                \[\|X-x_*\|^2,\|P_{\rm init}\|^2\in L^1(\nu),\quad P_{\rm init}\in L^1(\nu),\quad Z,\|Z\|^2\in L^1(\gamma_d).\]
                Corresponding Lean step

                hposI, hmomI, hmom1, hgaussI, hz1 and Integrable.op_fst_snd justify Fubini and all subsequent integral algebra.

                3. Use actual independence to kill the cross term

                For every fixed incoming momentum, the Gaussian mean is zero. Fubini is legal because the mixed inner product was proved integrable, hence its expectation under the product law vanishes without a centering assumption on Pinit.

                \[\mathbb E_{\nu\otimes\gamma_d}\langle P_{\rm init},Z\rangle=\mathbb E_\nu\langle P_{\rm init},\mathbb E_{\gamma_d}Z\rangle=0.\]
                Corresponding Lean step

                integral_strongDual_stdGaussian and integral_prod prove hcross0.

                4. Expand the refreshed square

                The coefficients satisfy a²=e^(−h) and sigma²=1−e^(−h). Expanding the Hilbert norm, integrating the four integrable terms, using the zero cross term and E‖Z‖²=d gives the exact identity.

                \[\|P_0\|^2=e^{-h}\|P_{\rm init}\|^2+2e^{-h/2}\sqrt{1-e^{-h}}\langle P_{\rm init},Z\rangle+(1-e^{-h})\|Z\|^2.\]
                Corresponding Lean step

                ha2, hs2, hexpand, hpieces and heq mirror this algebra and product integration.

                5. Derive the consumer-ready bound

                Because h≥0, 0<e^(−h)≤1. Replacing the damped momentum term by the incoming momentum square and applying the input budget yields M+(1−e^(−h))d. The extra dimension term must remain visible until the later paper-parameter absorption step.

                \[\mathbb E[\|X-x_*\|^2+e^{-h}\|P_{\rm init}\|^2]\le M.\]
                Corresponding Lean step

                hexp, hweighted and heq prove the final inequality. The focused test passes this result to picard_center_gradient_moment.

                Lean statement · partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment

                The source's independent Gaussian draw is represented definitionally by a product measure. The conclusion exposes measurability and integrability because the next Picard theorem requires them, and keeps Pinit distinct from the refreshed P0.

                theorem partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
    let μ := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
    let X : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => w.1.1
    let P0 : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2
    Measurable X ∧ Measurable P0 ∧
      Integrable (fun w => ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) =
        (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
        M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)

                ASTIS supplies the canonical Gaussian norm-square leaf and the paper-specific product-law adapter. Mathlib supplies product Fubini, Gaussian mean/covariance, Lp-to-integrability and Hilbert norm algebra.

                Braces mark parameters Lean can infer; square brackets request structures such as a measurable space or probability measure.                 theorem partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
    let μ := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
    let X : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => w.1.1
    let P0 : (E × E) × E → E := fun w => a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2
    Measurable X ∧ Measurable P0 ∧
      Integrable (fun w => ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) =
        (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
        M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  have hexp : Real.exp (-h) ≤ 1 := Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith)
  have hvar : 0 ≤ 1 - Real.exp (-h) := sub_nonneg.mpr hexp
  have ha2 : Real.exp (-h / 2) ^ 2 = Real.exp (-h) := by
    rw [pow_two, ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hs2 : Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) ^ 2 = 1 - Real.exp (-h) :=
    Real.sq_sqrt hvar
  have hposI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) ν := by
    apply hstateI.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards with s
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (sq_nonneg _)
  have hmomI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν := by
    apply hstateI.mono' (by fun_prop)
    filter_upwards with s
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_left (sq_nonneg _)
  have hmom1 : Integrable (fun s : E × E => s.2) ν :=
    MemLp.integrable (by norm_num : 1 ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞))
      ((memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm (by fun_prop)).2 hmomI)
  obtain ⟨hgaussI, hgauss⟩ :=
    integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian (E := E)
  have hz1 : Integrable (fun z : E => z) (stdGaussian E) := IsGaussian.integrable_id
  have hcross : Integrable
      (fun w : (E × E) × E => inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hmom1.op_fst_snd (by fun_prop)
      ⟨1, by intro x y; simpa using norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) x y⟩ hz1
  have hcross0 :
      (∫ w : (E × E) × E, inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 ∂ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) = 0 := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hcross]
    have hz (s : E × E) :
        (∫ z : E, inner ℝ s.2 z ∂stdGaussian E) = 0 :=
      integral_strongDual_stdGaussian (innerSL ℝ s.2)
    simp only [hz, integral_zero]
  have hposP := hposI.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hmomP := hmomI.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hgaussP := hgaussI.comp_snd ν
  have hcrossC : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
        inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hcross.const_mul _
  have hbase : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2)
      (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hposP.add (hmomP.const_mul _)
  have hbaseCross : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
        (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
          inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hbase.add hcrossC
  have hnoiseC : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hgaussP.const_mul _
  have hpieces : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
        (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
          inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 +
        (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2) (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hbaseCross.add hnoiseC
  have hexpand (w : (E × E) × E) :
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
          ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
            Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2 =
        ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖w.1.2‖ ^ 2 +
          (2 * Real.exp (-h / 2) * Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))) *
            inner ℝ w.1.2 w.2 +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [norm_add_sq_real, norm_smul, norm_smul, real_inner_smul_left,
      real_inner_smul_right]
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _),
      abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)]
    simp only [mul_pow, ha2, hs2]
    ring
  have houtI : Integrable (fun w : (E × E) × E =>
      ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
        ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
          Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2)
      (ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) := by
    simpa only [hexpand] using hpieces
  have heq :
      (∫ w : (E × E) × E,
          ‖w.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
            ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 +
              Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2‖ ^ 2
          ∂ν.prod (stdGaussian E)) =
        (∫ s : E × E,
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) +
          (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    simp_rw [hexpand]
    rw [integral_add hbaseCross hnoiseC,
      integral_add hbase hcrossC,
      integral_const_mul, hcross0, mul_zero, add_zero,
      integral_const_mul, integral_prod _ hgaussP]
    simp only [hgauss, integral_const]
    rw [integral_prod _ hbase]
    simp only [integral_const]
    simp
  have hweighted :
      (∫ s : E × E,
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν := by
        apply integral_mono (hposI.add (hmomI.const_mul _)) hstateI
        intro s
        change ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ≤
          ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2
        have hp : Real.exp (-h) * ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 := by
          simpa only [one_mul] using
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hexp (sq_nonneg ‖s.2‖)
        exact add_le_add_right hp (‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2)
      _ ≤ M := hstate
  refine ⟨by fun_prop, by fun_prop, houtI, heq, ?_⟩
  rw [heq]
  linarith

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PartialMomentumRefresh

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  Ordinary squared Wasserstein distance is at most six times the M-kappa squared transport value.

                  \[W_2^2(\mu,\nu)\le6W_{2,M_\kappa}^2(\mu,\nu).\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Lower-bound the twisted form

                    Cauchy--Schwarz and a completed square absorb the cross term without losing kappa.

                  2. 2Compare each coupling

                    The product max norm is bounded by the Euclidean sum of coordinate squares.

                  3. 3Remove near-optimal excess

                    Choose a twisted coupling within delta of the infimum and let delta vanish; no optimizer is assumed.

                  Lean proof · wassersteinDistance_sq_le_phaseWassersteinSq

                  Pointwise quadratic comparison, monotone integration, near-optimal coupling, epsilon closure.

                  Braces mark parameters Lean can infer; square brackets request structures such as a measurable space or probability measure. Named hypotheses are mathematical premises, not facts established by this declaration. Section parameters are described in the mathematical hypotheses above; the module link retains their exact source context.

                  theorem wassersteinDistance_sq_le_phaseWassersteinSq
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]
    {kappa : ℝ} (hkappa : 1 ≤ kappa) (mu nu : Measure (E × E)) :
    WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu ^ 2 ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal 6 * phaseWassersteinSq kappa mu nu := by
  rw [WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance_sq]
  apply ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add
  intro epsilon hepsilon hfinite
  let A : ℝ≥0∞ := ENNReal.ofReal 6
  let C : ℝ≥0∞ := phaseWassersteinSq kappa mu nu
  have hA0 : A ≠ 0 := by
    simp [A]
  have hAtop : A ≠ ⊤ := ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
  have hCtop : C < ⊤ := by
    rcases ENNReal.mul_lt_top_iff.mp hfinite with h | h | h
    · exact h.2
    · exact (hA0 h).elim
    · simpa [C, h]
  let delta : ℝ≥0∞ := (epsilon : ℝ≥0∞) / A
  have hdelta0 : delta ≠ 0 := by
    have hepsilon0 : (epsilon : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hepsilon.ne'
    exact (ENNReal.div_pos hepsilon0 hAtop).ne'
  have hstrict : C < C + delta :=
    ENNReal.lt_add_right hCtop.ne hdelta0
  obtain ⟨gamma, hgamma, hgammaCost⟩ :=
    Transport.exists_isCoupling_lintegral_lt_of_transportCost_lt
      (phaseCost (E := E) kappa) mu nu hstrict
  have hphaseMeas : Measurable (phaseCost (E := E) kappa) := by
    unfold phaseCost phaseQuadraticForm
    fun_prop
  calc
    Transport.transportCost (WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E × E)) mu nu ≤
        ∫⁻ z, WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E × E) z ∂gamma :=
      Transport.transportCost_le_lintegral_of_isCoupling _ mu nu gamma hgamma
    _ ≤ ∫⁻ z, A * phaseCost (E := E) kappa z ∂gamma := by
      apply lintegral_mono
      intro z
      exact quadraticCost_le_phaseCost hkappa z
    _ = A * ∫⁻ z, phaseCost (E := E) kappa z ∂gamma := by
      exact lintegral_const_mul _ hphaseMeas
    _ ≤ A * (C + delta) := by
      gcongr
    _ = A * C + (epsilon : ℝ≥0∞) := by
      rw [mul_add, show A * delta = (epsilon : ℝ≥0∞) by
        exact ENNReal.mul_div_cancel hA0 hAtop]
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal 6 * phaseWassersteinSq kappa mu nu +
        (epsilon : ℝ≥0∞) := rfl

                  theorem phase_state_second_moment_of_phaseWasserstein
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (nu reference : Measure (E × E)) (xstar : E) {kappa r Mx Mp : ℝ}
    (hkappa : 1 ≤ kappa)
    (hX : Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) reference)
    (hP : Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) reference)
    (hXbound : (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂reference) ≤ Mx)
    (hPbound : (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂reference) ≤ Mp)
    (hW : phaseWassersteinSq kappa nu reference ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ 2)) :
    Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) nu ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂nu) ≤
        2 * (Mx + Mp) + 24 * r ^ 2 := by
  have hsqrt : Real.sqrt 6 ^ 2 = 6 := Real.sq_sqrt (by norm_num)
  have hordinary : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance nu reference ^ 2 ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.sqrt 6 * r) ^ 2) := by
    refine (wassersteinDistance_sq_le_phaseWassersteinSq hkappa nu reference).trans ?_
    calc
      ENNReal.ofReal 6 * phaseWassersteinSq kappa nu reference ≤
          ENNReal.ofReal 6 * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ 2) := by gcongr
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.sqrt 6 * r) ^ 2) := by
        rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 6)]
        congr 1
        rw [mul_pow, hsqrt]
  have h := PhaseStateMoment.phase_state_second_moment_of_wasserstein
    nu reference xstar hX hP hXbound hPbound hordinary
  refine ⟨h.1, h.2.trans_eq ?_⟩
  rw [mul_pow, hsqrt]
  ring

end

                  Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                  Gaussian smoothing adds exactly one noise second moment

                  AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PhaseReferenceMoment.gaussianSmoothing_position_second_moment · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  Convolving a probability law with an independent centered isotropic Gaussian of scale sigma increases its second moment about xstar by exactly sigma squared times the dimension.

                  \[\int\|y-x_\star\|^2\,d(\mu*\mathsf N(0,\sigma^2I))(y)=\int\|x-x_\star\|^2\,d\mu(x)+\sigma^2d.\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Expose the independent product

                    Gaussian smoothing is the pushforward of an independent pair (X,Z) under X+sigma Z.

                  2. 2Expand the square

                    Separate the old position energy, the centered cross term, and the Gaussian energy.

                  3. 3Justify and cancel the cross term

                    The two L2 assumptions imply integrability of the product inner product; independence and E Z=0 then make its integral zero.

                  4. 4Insert the Gaussian trace

                    The coordinate-free standard-Gaussian second moment is the real dimension.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space.
                  • mu is a probability measure.
                  • The squared distance to xstar is mu-integrable.
                  • sigma is the Gaussian standard-deviation scale; the paper later uses sigma=sqrt(eta).

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Expose the independent product

                  Gaussian smoothing is the pushforward of an independent pair (X,Z) under X+sigma Z.

                  \[\mu*\mathsf N(0,\sigma^2I)=(\mu\otimes\gamma)_\#[(x,z)\mapsto x+\sigma z].\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  gaussianSmoothing, scaledStdGaussian, Measure.map_prod_map and Measure.map_map.

                  2. Expand the square

                  Separate the old position energy, the centered cross term, and the Gaussian energy.

                  \[\|X+\sigma Z-x_\star\|^2=\|X-x_\star\|^2+2\sigma\langle X-x_\star,Z\rangle+\sigma^2\|Z\|^2.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  norm_add_sq_real after an explicit subtraction identity.

                  3. Justify and cancel the cross term

                  The two L2 assumptions imply integrability of the product inner product; independence and E Z=0 then make its integral zero.

                  \[\mathbb E\langle X-x_\star,Z\rangle=\mathbb E\langle X-x_\star,\mathbb EZ\rangle=0.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  MemLp.integrable, Integrable.op_fst_snd, integral_prod and integral_strongDual_stdGaussian.

                  4. Insert the Gaussian trace

                  The coordinate-free standard-Gaussian second moment is the real dimension.

                  \[\mathbb E\|Z\|^2=d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  StdGaussianMoment.integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian.

                  Lean verification

                  The exact proposition and proof begin folded so the mathematical argument remains the primary reading path.

    Integrable (fun y : E => ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2) piSigma ∧
      (∫ y : E, ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂piSigma) =

                  theorem gaussianSmoothing_position_second_moment
    (mu : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (xstar : E) (sigma : ℝ)
    (hpos : Integrable (fun x : E => ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2) mu) :
    let piSigma := gaussianSmoothing mu sigma
    Integrable (fun y : E => ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2) piSigma ∧
      (∫ y : E, ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂piSigma) =
        (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) +
          sigma ^ 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  classical
  let A : E × E → E := fun w => w.1 + sigma • w.2
  let piSigma := gaussianSmoothing mu sigma
  have hA : Measurable A := by fun_prop
  have hprod :
      mu.prod (scaledStdGaussian (E := E) sigma) =
        (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)).map (Prod.map id (fun z : E => sigma • z)) := by
    simpa only [Measure.map_id, scaledStdGaussian] using
      Measure.map_prod_map mu (stdGaussian E) measurable_id
        (by fun_prop : Measurable (fun z : E => sigma • z))
  have hpiSigma : piSigma = (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)).map A := by
    dsimp [piSigma, gaussianSmoothing,
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.CommonNoiseContraction.addNoise]
    rw [hprod, Measure.map_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)]
    rfl
  have hx1 : Integrable (fun x : E => x - xstar) mu :=
    MemLp.integrable (by norm_num : 1 ≤ (2 : ℝ≥0∞))
      ((memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm (by fun_prop)).2 hpos)
  obtain ⟨hgauss, hgaussIntegral⟩ :=
    integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian (E := E)
  have hz1 : Integrable (fun z : E => z) (stdGaussian E) :=
    IsGaussian.integrable_id
  have hcross : Integrable
      (fun w : E × E => inner ℝ (w.1 - xstar) w.2)
      (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)) :=
    hx1.op_fst_snd (by fun_prop)
      ⟨1, by intro x y; simpa using norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) x y⟩ hz1
  have hcross0 :
      (∫ w : E × E, inner ℝ (w.1 - xstar) w.2
          ∂mu.prod (stdGaussian E)) = 0 := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hcross]
    have hz (x : E) :
        (∫ z : E, inner ℝ (x - xstar) z ∂stdGaussian E) = 0 :=
      integral_strongDual_stdGaussian (innerSL ℝ (x - xstar))
    simp only [hz, integral_zero]
  have hposP := hpos.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hgaussP := hgauss.comp_snd mu
  have hcrossC : Integrable (fun w : E × E =>
      (2 * sigma) * inner ℝ (w.1 - xstar) w.2)
      (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hcross.const_mul _
  have hbase : Integrable (fun w : E × E =>
      ‖w.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + (2 * sigma) * inner ℝ (w.1 - xstar) w.2)
      (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hposP.add hcrossC
  have hnoise : Integrable (fun w : E × E => sigma ^ 2 * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2)
      (mu.prod (stdGaussian E)) := hgaussP.const_mul _
  have hpieces := hbase.add hnoise
  have hexpand (w : E × E) :
      ‖A w - xstar‖ ^ 2 =
        ‖w.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
          (2 * sigma) * inner ℝ (w.1 - xstar) w.2 +
          sigma ^ 2 * ‖w.2‖ ^ 2 := by
    have hsub : A w - xstar = (w.1 - xstar) + sigma • w.2 := by

    rw [hsub, norm_add_sq_real, norm_smul, real_inner_smul_right]
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs]
    simp only [mul_pow, sq_abs]

                  Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                  The actual SPHMC product reference has controlled phase energy

                  AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PhaseReferenceMoment.phaseReference_second_moment · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  The product of the smoothed position law and independent standard-Gaussian momentum is a probability law with exact coordinate moments and an explicit combined phase-energy bound.

                  \[\mathbb E_{\Pi_\sigma}[\|X-x_\star\|^2+\|P\|^2]\le M+(\sigma^2+1)d.\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Construct the phase law

                    Use the actual product measure, not two unrelated marginal assumptions.

                  2. 2Integrate the position coordinate

                    The second coordinate has total mass one, so the product integral is the smoothing identity.

                  3. 3Integrate the momentum coordinate

                    The first marginal has total mass one and the momentum is standard Gaussian.

                  4. 4Add the two energies

                    Product integrability legitimizes splitting the integral before applying the supplied base bound.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • The hypotheses of the smoothing theorem.
                  • The original position moment is bounded above by M.

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Construct the phase law

                  Use the actual product measure, not two unrelated marginal assumptions.

                  \[\Pi_\sigma=(\mu*\mathsf N(0,\sigma^2I))\otimes\mathsf N(0,I).\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  piSigma.prod (stdGaussian E), with an explicit probability instance for the smoothing pushforward.

                  2. Integrate the position coordinate

                  The second coordinate has total mass one, so the product integral is the smoothing identity.

                  \[\mathbb E_{\Pi_\sigma}\|X-x_\star\|^2=\mathbb E_\mu\|X-x_\star\|^2+\sigma^2d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Integrable.comp_fst, integral_prod and probReal_univ.

                  3. Integrate the momentum coordinate

                  The first marginal has total mass one and the momentum is standard Gaussian.

                  \[\mathbb E_{\Pi_\sigma}\|P\|^2=d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Integrable.comp_snd and the standard-Gaussian moment theorem.

                  4. Add the two energies

                  Product integrability legitimizes splitting the integral before applying the supplied base bound.

                  \[(M+\sigma^2d)+d=M+(\sigma^2+1)d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  integral_add followed by linarith.

                  theorem phaseReference_second_moment
    (mu : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (xstar : E) (sigma M : ℝ)
    (hpos : Integrable (fun x : E => ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2) mu)
    (hposBound : (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) ≤ M) :
    let piSigma := gaussianSmoothing mu sigma
    let PiSigma := piSigma.prod (stdGaussian E)
    IsProbabilityMeasure PiSigma ∧
      Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) =
        (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) +
          sigma ^ 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) = Module.finrank ℝ E ∧
      Integrable
        (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) ≤
        M + (sigma ^ 2 + 1) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)

                  theorem phaseReference_second_moment
    (mu : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure mu] (xstar : E) (sigma M : ℝ)
    (hpos : Integrable (fun x : E => ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2) mu)
    (hposBound : (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) ≤ M) :
    let piSigma := gaussianSmoothing mu sigma
    let PiSigma := piSigma.prod (stdGaussian E)
    IsProbabilityMeasure PiSigma ∧
      Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) =
        (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) +
          sigma ^ 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) = Module.finrank ℝ E ∧
      Integrable
        (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) PiSigma ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂PiSigma) ≤
        M + (sigma ^ 2 + 1) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let piSigma := gaussianSmoothing mu sigma
  have hposition :
      Integrable (fun y : E => ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2) piSigma ∧
        (∫ y : E, ‖y - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂piSigma) =
          (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) +
            sigma ^ 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    simpa only [piSigma] using
      gaussianSmoothing_position_second_moment mu xstar sigma hpos
  obtain ⟨hgauss, hgaussIntegral⟩ :=
    integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian (E := E)
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure piSigma := by
    dsimp [piSigma, gaussianSmoothing,
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.CommonNoiseContraction.addNoise]
    exact Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map
      (by fun_prop : AEMeasurable (fun p : E × E => p.1 + p.2)
        (mu.prod (scaledStdGaussian (E := E) sigma)))
  have hX := hposition.1.comp_fst (stdGaussian E)
  have hP := hgauss.comp_snd piSigma
  have hXI :
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂piSigma.prod (stdGaussian E)) =
        (∫ x : E, ‖x - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) +
          sigma ^ 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hX]
    simp only [integral_const, probReal_univ, one_smul, hposition.2]
  have hPI :
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂piSigma.prod (stdGaussian E)) =
        Module.finrank ℝ E := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hP]
    simp only [hgaussIntegral, integral_const, probReal_univ, one_smul]
  refine ⟨inferInstance, hX, hP, hXI, hPI, hX.add hP, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_add hX hP, hXI, hPI]
  linarith

                  Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                  Wasserstein distance transfers a Lipschitz observable's second moment

                  AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WassersteinLipschitzMoment.of_wassersteinDistance_sq_le · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  The observable remains square-integrable under μ, and its μ second moment is bounded by twice its reference second moment plus 2b²r².

                  \[W_2^2(\mu,\nu)\le r^2\Longrightarrow \int\|g\|^2d\mu\le 2\int\|g\|^2d\nu+2b^2r^2.\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Choose an almost-optimal coupling

                    For every s>r², the definition of transport cost supplies a coupling whose quadratic cost is below s. Optimal-plan existence is unnecessary.

                  2. 2Dominate the transported observable

                    Lipschitz continuity and the quadratic two-term inequality control the first-coordinate observable by an integrable reference term plus coupling displacement.

                  3. 3Use the exact marginals

                    The coordinate projections of γ preserve μ and ν, so the two coupling integrals are exactly the desired marginal moments.

                  4. 4Remove the excess cost

                    The bound holds for every s>r². Applying it at a controlled positive excess and letting that excess be arbitrary gives the closed r² bound.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • E is a second-countable Borel normed additive group and F is a normed additive group.
                  • g:E→F is b-Lipschitz and its squared norm is integrable under the reference law ν.
                  • The squared extended-real Wasserstein distance from μ to ν is at most ofReal(r²).

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Choose an almost-optimal coupling

                  For every s>r², the definition of transport cost supplies a coupling whose quadratic cost is below s. Optimal-plan existence is unnecessary.

                  \[\exists\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu):\int\|x-y\|^2d\gamma\le s.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  wassersteinDistance_sq and exists_isCoupling_lintegral_lt_of_transportCost_lt.

                  2. Dominate the transported observable

                  Lipschitz continuity and the quadratic two-term inequality control the first-coordinate observable by an integrable reference term plus coupling displacement.

                  \[\|g(x)\|^2\le2\|g(y)\|^2+2b^2\|x-y\|^2.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  The private pointwise bound and Integrable.mono' establish integrability before integral comparison.

                  3. Use the exact marginals

                  The coordinate projections of γ preserve μ and ν, so the two coupling integrals are exactly the desired marginal moments.

                  \[(\mathrm{fst})_\#\gamma=\mu,\quad(\mathrm{snd})_\#\gamma=\nu.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  CouplingQuadraticIntegrability.measurePreserving_fst/snd_of_isCoupling.

                  4. Remove the excess cost

                  The bound holds for every s>r². Applying it at a controlled positive excess and letting that excess be arbitrary gives the closed r² bound.

                  \[\forall\varepsilon>0,\ I_\mu\le2I_\nu+2b^2r^2+\varepsilon.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  le_of_forall_pos_le_add and real algebra close the infimum argument.

    {g : E → F} {b : ℝ≥0} {r : ℝ} (hg : LipschitzWith b g)
    (hi : Integrable (fun x => ‖g x‖ ^ 2) nu)
    (hw : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu ^ 2 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ 2)) :
    Integrable (fun x => ‖g x‖ ^ 2) mu ∧
      (∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) ≤

Named hypotheses are mathematical premises, not facts established by this declaration. Section parameters are described in the mathematical hypotheses above; the module link retains their exact source context.

                  theorem of_wassersteinDistance_sq_le {mu nu : Measure E}
    {g : E → F} {b : ℝ≥0} {r : ℝ} (hg : LipschitzWith b g)
    (hi : Integrable (fun x => ‖g x‖ ^ 2) nu)
    (hw : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu ^ 2 ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ 2)) :
    Integrable (fun x => ‖g x‖ ^ 2) mu ∧
      (∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) ≤
        2 * (∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 ∂nu) + 2 * (b : ℝ) ^ 2 * r ^ 2 := by
  have hall (s : ℝ) (hs : r ^ 2 < s) :
      Integrable (fun x => ‖g x‖ ^ 2) mu ∧
        (∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 ∂mu) ≤
          2 * (∫ x, ‖g x‖ ^ 2 ∂nu) + 2 * (b : ℝ) ^ 2 * s := by
    have hs0 : 0 < s := (sq_nonneg r).trans_lt hs
    have hcost : Transport.transportCost
        (WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E)) mu nu < ENNReal.ofReal s := by
      rw [← WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance_sq]
      exact hw.trans_lt ((ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff hs0).2 hs)
    obtain ⟨gamma, hgamma, hgammaCost⟩ :=
      Transport.exists_isCoupling_lintegral_lt_of_transportCost_lt
        (WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (E := E)) mu nu hcost
    exact of_isCoupling hg hi hgamma hs0.le hgammaCost.le
  refine ⟨(hall (r ^ 2 + 1) (by linarith)).1, ?_⟩
  apply le_of_forall_pos_le_add
  intro epsilon hepsilon
  have hden : 0 < 2 * (b : ℝ) ^ 2 + 1 := by positivity
  have hdelta : 0 < epsilon / (2 * (b : ℝ) ^ 2 + 1) := div_pos hepsilon hden
  have hbound := (hall (r ^ 2 + epsilon / (2 * (b : ℝ) ^ 2 + 1)) (by linarith)).2
  have heq := div_mul_cancel₀ epsilon hden.ne'
  nlinarith

                  Ordinary-Wasserstein control gives an SPHMC phase-state moment

                  AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PhaseStateMoment.phase_state_second_moment_of_wasserstein · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  The incoming phase energy is integrable and at most 2(Mx+Mp)+4r².

                  \[\mathbb E_\nu[\|X-x_\star\|^2+\|P\|^2]\le2(M_X+M_P)+4r^2.\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Position is a one-Lipschitz observable

                    For the max product metric, projecting to position and subtracting xstar cannot increase distance.

                  2. 2Momentum is a one-Lipschitz observable

                    The second product projection is one-Lipschitz for the same metric.

                  3. 3Transfer both moments

                    Apply the shared theorem independently to position and momentum, preserving both integrability conclusions.

                  4. 4Add only after integrability

                    Bochner integral additivity is now legal; adding the bounds gives the combined phase energy.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • The reference phase law has integrable position and momentum squares, bounded respectively by Mx and Mp.
                  • The incoming law is within ordinary squared W2 radius r² of the reference law.
                  • The state space is finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel; completeness is not needed by this theorem.

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Position is a one-Lipschitz observable

                  For the max product metric, projecting to position and subtracting xstar cannot increase distance.

                  \[g_X(x,p)=x-x_\star,\quad\operatorname{Lip}(g_X)\le1.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul and Prod.dist_eq.

                  2. Momentum is a one-Lipschitz observable

                  The second product projection is one-Lipschitz for the same metric.

                  \[g_P(x,p)=p,\quad\operatorname{Lip}(g_P)\le1.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  LipschitzWith.prod_snd.

                  3. Transfer both moments

                  Apply the shared theorem independently to position and momentum, preserving both integrability conclusions.

                  \[I_X\le2M_X+2r^2,\qquad I_P\le2M_P+2r^2.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Two calls to of_wassersteinDistance_sq_le.

                  4. Add only after integrability

                  Bochner integral additivity is now legal; adding the bounds gives the combined phase energy.

                  \[I_X+I_P\le2(M_X+M_P)+4r^2.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Integrable.add, integral_add, and linear arithmetic.

    (hX : Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2) reference)

    (hXbound : (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 ∂reference) ≤ Mx)
    (hPbound : (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂reference) ≤ Mp)
    (hW : WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance nu reference ^ 2 ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ 2)) :
    Integrable (fun z : E × E => ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2) nu ∧
      (∫ z : E × E, ‖z.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 ∂nu) ≤
        2 * (Mx + Mp) + 4 * r ^ 2 := by
  have hXlip : LipschitzWith 1 (fun z : E × E => z.1 - xstar) := by
    refine LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul ?_
    intro a b
    rw [NNReal.coe_one, one_mul, Prod.dist_eq]
    simpa only [dist_eq_norm, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using
      (le_max_left (dist a.1 b.1) (dist a.2 b.2))
  have hPlip : LipschitzWith 1 (fun z : E × E => z.2) :=
    LipschitzWith.prod_snd
  have hXt := WassersteinLipschitzMoment.of_wassersteinDistance_sq_le hXlip hX hW
  have hPt := WassersteinLipschitzMoment.of_wassersteinDistance_sq_le hPlip hP hW
  refine ⟨hXt.1.add hPt.1, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_add hXt.1 hPt.1]
  norm_num at hXt hPt
  linarith

end

                  SPHMC D.7 proof edge: two Picard layers from a phase-state moment

                  Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib expands one conditional two-layer moment edge; it is not the authors' original wording, the whole equation D.7, Lemma D.4, equation D.8 or an endorsement.

                  arXiv:2609.06906v1 · Appendix D.2, Lemma D.4, equation D.7, layer argument on lines 2177–2181 · faithful paraphrase

                  Complete source statement (Samplinglib restatement)

                  Conditional on the separate run-wide phase-state second-moment estimate and the Chebyshev–Lobatto integrated-weight row bound, the actual stopped approximate-proximal computation used by the first Picard layer has integrable gradient queries, and those moments propagate through the finite weighted update to every second-layer center. All measurability and integrability obligations are explicit, and marginal Gaussian second moments suffice.

                  • Finite-dimensional Euclidean-compatible Borel space; C² normalized Hessian bounds kappa⁻¹I≼D²V≼I and a minimizer x* with ∇V(x*)=0.
                  • A probability-space realization of one phase with E[‖X−x*‖²+‖P₀‖²]≤M for the post-refresh momentum P₀, including integrability; |t_i|≤1. The refresh adapter from the repeated-chain state remains separate.
                  • Measurable innovations with integrable squared norm and E‖G_j‖²≤d; no independence premise is used in this conditional edge.
                  • Absolute integrated-weight row sum at most S and parameters 0<eta≤c<1, eps>0.

                  Random first-layer query bound

                  \[B=6M+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(q(Y_j^0)+\sqrt\eta G_j)\|^2\le B.\]

                  Second-layer center-gradient bound

                  \[Y_i^1=Y_i^0-\sum_j\omega_{ij}Z_j^0,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^1)\|^2\le4M+2S^2B.\]

                  Samplinglib mathematical lesson

                  Second moments through the two Picard query layers

                  AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PicardCenterMoment.picard_center_gradient_moment · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  Define the first Picard centers Y⁰_i=X+t_iP₀. The actual stopped gradient-descent proximal program constructs measurable exact proximal points p, stopping indices N and returned points q, with p(y)+eta∇V(p(y))=y, ‖q(y)−p(y)‖≤eps and an exact finite-interpreter return equation. Define Z⁰_j=∇V(q(Y⁰_j)+sqrt(eta)G_j) and Y¹_i=Y⁰_i−Σ_j omega_ij Z⁰_j. Then all three displayed squared-gradient fields are integrable and obey the following explicit bounds. Center moments are established internally as the dominators, but are not separate public conclusions.

                  \[\begin{gathered}B=6M+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^0)\|^2\le 2M,\\ \mathbb E\|Z_j^0\|^2\le B,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^1)\|^2\le 4M+2S^2B.\end{gathered}\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Control the first centers

                    Because |t_i|≤1, expanding Y⁰_i−x*=(X−x*)+t_iP and using (a+b)²≤2a²+2b² gives an integrable pointwise dominator. The state premise can therefore be integrated before any gradient estimate is used.

                  2. 2Use genuine smoothness to control gradients

                    The upper Hessian bound and C² regularity yield a genuinely 1-Lipschitz gradient. Since ∇V(x*)=0, the gradient norm is bounded by distance to x*. This also supplies measurability, so domination gives integrability rather than merely a numerical inequality.

                  3. 3Relate the actual approximate query to the exact prox

                    The existing execution theorem returns the actual finite stopped iterate q together with ‖q−p‖≤eps. The exact proximal map p is nonexpansive: subtract its two optimality equations and pair with p(y)−p(z); monotonicity of ∇V makes the extra term nonnegative. As x* solves its own proximal equation, p(x*)=x*.

                  4. 4Bound every random proximal-gradient query

                    Apply the 1-Lipschitz gradient estimate after adding sqrt(eta)G_j, then use (a+b+c)²≤3(a²+b²+c²). Only the marginal second moment of G_j enters, so no independence or joint Gaussian construction is needed here.

                  5. 5Propagate through the weighted second layer

                    A weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality bounds the square of the finite update by its absolute row sum times the correspondingly weighted query moments. Integrating and using Σ_j|omega_ij|≤S yields S²B. Combining this update with the first-center bound, then using the gradient-distance inequality once more, gives the layer-1 result.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. V:E→R is C², kappa≥1, and kappa⁻¹‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤‖v‖² for every x,v.
                  • On an arbitrary probability space, X and the post-refresh momentum P₀ used by Algorithm 3.1 are measurable and E[‖X−x*‖²+‖P₀‖²]≤M, with the integrability stated separately. A future adapter must derive this from the repeated-chain state estimate and the refresh step. The point x* is a genuine minimizer witness through ∇V(x*)=0.
                  • The finite node family satisfies |t_i|≤1. Each innovation G_j is measurable, has integrable squared norm and E‖G_j‖²≤dim(E). Independence between nodes, X, P and G is not required for this edge.
                  • The integrated interpolation weights satisfy Σ_j|omega_ij|≤S. The step parameters obey 0<eta≤c<1 and eps>0, so the existing finite stopped proximal program applies.

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Control the first centers

                  Because |t_i|≤1, expanding Y⁰_i−x*=(X−x*)+t_iP and using (a+b)²≤2a²+2b² gives an integrable pointwise dominator. The state premise can therefore be integrated before any gradient estimate is used.

                  \[\|Y_i^0-x_*\|^2\le2(\|X-x_*\|^2+\|P\|^2),\qquad \mathbb E\|Y_i^0-x_*\|^2\le2M.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  hY0bound, hY0I and hY0int establish the pointwise inequality, Bochner integrability and integral bound in that order.

                  2. Use genuine smoothness to control gradients

                  The upper Hessian bound and C² regularity yield a genuinely 1-Lipschitz gradient. Since ∇V(x*)=0, the gradient norm is bounded by distance to x*. This also supplies measurability, so domination gives integrability rather than merely a numerical inequality.

                  \[\|\nabla V(y)\|=\|\nabla V(y)-\nabla V(x_*)\|\le\|y-x_*\|,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^0)\|^2\le2M.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  The shared quadratic-regularization theorem produces hLip; hgrad, hgradI and hgradInt apply it without treating totalized fderiv as differentiability.

                  3. Relate the actual approximate query to the exact prox

                  The existing execution theorem returns the actual finite stopped iterate q together with ‖q−p‖≤eps. The exact proximal map p is nonexpansive: subtract its two optimality equations and pair with p(y)−p(z); monotonicity of ∇V makes the extra term nonnegative. As x* solves its own proximal equation, p(x*)=x*.

                  \[\|p(y)-p(z)\|\le\|y-z\|,\qquad p(x_*)=x_*,\qquad \|q(y)-x_*\|\le\|y-x_*\|+\varepsilon.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  hpLip and hpstar are proved from hall and strong-convex gradient monotonicity. The theorem deliberately does not call the older eta≤1/2 Lipschitz wrapper, because D.7 only assumes 0<eta≤c<1.

                  4. Bound every random proximal-gradient query

                  Apply the 1-Lipschitz gradient estimate after adding sqrt(eta)G_j, then use (a+b+c)²≤3(a²+b²+c²). Only the marginal second moment of G_j enters, so no independence or joint Gaussian construction is needed here.

                  \[\|Z_j^0\|^2\le3(\|Y_j^0-x_*\|^2+\varepsilon^2+\eta\|G_j\|^2),\qquad \mathbb E\|Z_j^0\|^2\le6M+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d=B.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  hZbound gives the pointwise estimate; hZdomI and hZI make the integrability obligation explicit; hZint integrates it using the probability normalization.

                  5. Propagate through the weighted second layer

                  A weighted Cauchy–Schwarz inequality bounds the square of the finite update by its absolute row sum times the correspondingly weighted query moments. Integrating and using Σ_j|omega_ij|≤S yields S²B. Combining this update with the first-center bound, then using the gradient-distance inequality once more, gives the layer-1 result.

                  \[\left\|\sum_j\omega_{ij}Z_j^0\right\|^2\le\left(\sum_j|\omega_{ij}|\right)\sum_j|\omega_{ij}|\|Z_j^0\|^2,\quad \mathbb E\left\|\sum_j\omega_{ij}Z_j^0\right\|^2\le S^2B,\quad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(Y_i^1)\|^2\le4M+2S^2B.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  weighted_sum_norm_sq_le, hweighted, hsumSqI and hsumInt handle the finite sum; hY1I, hY1int and hgrad1I complete the second layer.

                  AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PicardInputLaw.partial_refresh_with_picard_innovations · theorem · Teaching coverage

                  Read this first

                  Mathematical statement

                  On the nested product of the incoming law, a fresh standard Gaussian, and a finite product of standard Gaussians, the refreshed X and P0 and every Picard innovation G_j are measurable and square-integrable with their exact consumer-ready moment bounds.

                  \[B_{\rm refresh}=M+(1-e^{-h})d,\qquad \mathbb E\|G_j^{[0]}\|^2=d.\]

                  Proof roadmap

                  1. 1Build the probability space

                    The nested product measure represents freshness of the first refresh Gaussian and the first Picard innovation array.

                  2. 2Reuse the refresh calculation

                    The previous theorem already proves measurability, integrability, and the corrected OU moment budget; product integration lifts it unchanged over the extra innovation array.

                  3. 3Read each Gaussian coordinate

                    Evaluation at j is measurable. Finite-product marginal integration returns the original standard Gaussian law, so every coordinate has exactly dimension d as its squared-norm moment.

                  4. 4Feed the real variables to the next theorem

                    The focused test passes the product-law coordinate projections to the two-layer Picard moment theorem, and separately checks a nondegenerate one-dimensional Gaussian coordinate moment.

                  Full assumptions and notation

                  All objects and hypotheses

                  • The incoming phase-state law is a probability measure with an integrable combined square bounded by M≥0.
                  • The phase length is nonnegative and the Picard index type is finite.
                  • E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space.

                  Mathematical proof

                  1. Build the probability space

                  The nested product measure represents freshness of the first refresh Gaussian and the first Picard innovation array.

                  \[\mu=(\nu\otimes\gamma_d)\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in[J]}\gamma_d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Measure.prod constructs the refresh factor and Measure.pi constructs the finite innovation array.

                  2. Reuse the refresh calculation

                  The previous theorem already proves measurability, integrability, and the corrected OU moment budget; product integration lifts it unchanged over the extra innovation array.

                  \[\mathbb E_\mu[\|X-x_*\|^2+\|P_0\|^2]\le B_{\rm refresh}.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Integrable.comp_fst and integral_prod transport the established result.

                  3. Read each Gaussian coordinate

                  Evaluation at j is measurable. Finite-product marginal integration returns the original standard Gaussian law, so every coordinate has exactly dimension d as its squared-norm moment.

                  \[G_j(w)=w_{\rm array}(j),\quad \mathbb E\|G_j\|^2=d.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  integrable_comp_eval and integral_comp_eval are the pinned Mathlib APIs.

                  4. Feed the real variables to the next theorem

                  The focused test passes the product-law coordinate projections to the two-layer Picard moment theorem, and separately checks a nondegenerate one-dimensional Gaussian coordinate moment.

                  \[(X,P_0,(G_j)_j)\longrightarrow\text{PicardCenterMoment}.\]
                  Corresponding Lean step

                  Tests.SmoothedPicardHMCPartialMomentumRefresh checks symbolic API composition in dimension zero and the exact positive-dimensional Gaussian moment in E=R.

                  Lean statement · partial_refresh_with_picard_innovations

                  The nested lets expose the exact probability law and random variables, while the conjunction returns every measurability and integrability premise required downstream.

                  Braces mark parameters Lean can infer; square brackets request structures such as a measurable space or probability measure. Named hypotheses are mathematical premises, not facts established by this declaration. Section parameters are described in the mathematical hypotheses above; the module link retains their exact source context.

                  theorem partial_refresh_with_picard_innovations
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
    let μRefresh := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
    let γι := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
    let μ := μRefresh.prod γι
    let X : (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E := fun w => w.1.1.1
    let P0 : (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E :=
      fun w => a • w.1.1.2 + sigma • w.1.2
    let G : ι → (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E := fun j w => w.2 j
    let BRefresh := M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    0 ≤ BRefresh ∧
      Measurable X ∧ Measurable P0 ∧
      Integrable (fun w => ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤ BRefresh ∧
      (∀ j, Measurable (G j)) ∧
      (∀ j, Integrable (fun w => ‖G j w‖ ^ 2) μ) ∧
      (∀ j, (∫ w, ‖G j w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) = (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ))

                  theorem partial_refresh_with_picard_innovations
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 ≤ h) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖s.2‖ ^ 2 ∂ν) ≤ M) :
    let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
    let μRefresh := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
    let γι := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
    let μ := μRefresh.prod γι
    let X : (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E := fun w => w.1.1.1
    let P0 : (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E :=
      fun w => a • w.1.1.2 + sigma • w.1.2
    let G : ι → (((E × E) × E) × (ι → E)) → E := fun j w => w.2 j
    let BRefresh := M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    0 ≤ BRefresh ∧
      Measurable X ∧ Measurable P0 ∧
      Integrable (fun w => ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2) μ ∧
      (∫ w, ‖X w - xstar‖ ^ 2 + ‖P0 w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤ BRefresh ∧
      (∀ j, Measurable (G j)) ∧
      (∀ j, Integrable (fun w => ‖G j w‖ ^ 2) μ) ∧
      (∀ j, (∫ w, ‖G j w‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) = (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  obtain ⟨hX, hP0, hrefreshI, hrefreshEq, hrefresh⟩ :=
    PartialMomentumRefresh.partial_momentum_refresh_second_moment
      ν xstar hh hstateI hstate
  let μRefresh := ν.prod (stdGaussian E)
  let γι := Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
  have hvar : 0 ≤ 1 - Real.exp (-h) :=
    sub_nonneg.mpr (Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith))
  have hB : 0 ≤ M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) :=
    add_nonneg hM (mul_nonneg hvar (Nat.cast_nonneg _))
  have hrefreshOuter : Integrable
      (fun w : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E) =>
        ‖w.1.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
          ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.1.2 +
            Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.1.2‖ ^ 2)
      (μRefresh.prod γι) := hrefreshI.comp_fst γι
  have hrefreshOuterInt :
      (∫ w : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E),
          ‖w.1.1.1 - xstar‖ ^ 2 +
            ‖Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.1.2 +
              Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.1.2‖ ^ 2
          ∂μRefresh.prod γι) ≤
        M + (1 - Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    rw [integral_prod _ hrefreshOuter]
    simpa [γι, μRefresh] using hrefresh
  obtain ⟨hgaussI, hgauss⟩ :=
    integrable_norm_sq_and_integral_stdGaussian (E := E)
  have hcoordI (j : ι) : Integrable (fun z : ι → E => ‖z j‖ ^ 2) γι :=
    by
      simpa [γι] using
        (integrable_comp_eval (X := fun _ : ι => E)
          (μ := fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E) (i := j) hgaussI)
  have hcoordOuterI (j : ι) : Integrable
      (fun w : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E) => ‖w.2 j‖ ^ 2)
      (μRefresh.prod γι) := (hcoordI j).comp_snd μRefresh
  have hcoordOuter (j : ι) :
      (∫ w : ((E × E) × E) × (ι → E), ‖w.2 j‖ ^ 2
          ∂μRefresh.prod γι) = (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) := by
    rw [integral_prod _ (hcoordOuterI j)]
    simp [μRefresh, γι,
      integral_comp_eval (X := fun _ : ι => E) (μ := fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)
        (i := j) hgaussI.aestronglyMeasurable,
      hgauss]
  exact ⟨hB, by fun_prop, by fun_prop, hrefreshOuter, hrefreshOuterInt,
    fun _ => by fun_prop, hcoordOuterI, hcoordOuter⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PicardInputLaw
